Create a Margot Plot with Proper Multiplicity Correction

Source: R/margot_plot.R
margot_plot.Rd

Create coordinated plots, tables and text from supplied effect estimates and confidence intervals, with the requested multiplicity adjustment. Model-scale estimates and sensitivity quantities remain separate from reported unit conversions.

Usage

margot_plot(
  .data,
  type = c("RD", "RR"),
  order = c("alphabetical", "magnitude_desc", "magnitude_asc", "evaluebound_desc",
    "evaluebound_asc", "custom", "default"),
  custom_order = NULL,
  title_binary = NULL,
  include_coefficients = TRUE,
  standardize_label = c("NZ", "US", "none"),
  e_val_bound_threshold = 1.2,
  adjust = c("none", "bonferroni", "holm", "BH"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  ...,
  options = list(),
  label_mapping = NULL,
  save_output = FALSE,
  use_timestamp = FALSE,
  base_filename = "margot_plot_output",
  prefix = NULL,
  save_path = here::here("push_mods"),
  original_df = NULL,
  bold_rows = FALSE,
  rename_cols = FALSE,
  col_renames = list(`E-Value` = "E_Value", `E-Value bound` = "E_Val_bound"),
  rename_ate = FALSE,
  rename_evalue = FALSE,
  scale_info = NULL,
  category_rule = c("interval", "interval_and_evalue"),
  e_val_bound_comparison = c(">", ">="),
  e_val_bound_conversion = c("exact", "rounded"),
  order_direction = c("top_to_bottom", "bottom_to_top"),
  table_columns = c("report", "legacy")
)

Arguments

.data

data frame containing causal effect estimates with columns for effect sizes, confidence intervals, E-values and E-value bounds

type

character. type of effect estimate: "RD" (risk difference) or "RR" (risk ratio)

order

Outcome ordering rule. The first outcome in the ordering is drawn at the top of the plot (see `order_direction`), and the table and text follow the graph from top to bottom. `"magnitude_desc"` puts the largest absolute effect at the top; `"magnitude_asc"` the smallest; `"evaluebound_desc"` the largest E-value bound; `"alphabetical"` runs A to Z down the plot; `"custom"` follows `custom_order` from the top.

custom_order

Outcome display labels in the requested order, first at the top of the plot (with the default `order_direction`).

title_binary

Retained compatibility argument.

include_coefficients

Whether to print numerical coefficients on the plot.

standardize_label

Axis-label convention: New Zealand, US, or no standardisation label.

e_val_bound_threshold

Reporting threshold for the E-value bound. By default it sets only the E-value flag reported beside each estimate (table column and prose); it does not change the plotted category. Under `category_rule = "interval_and_evalue"` it also gates the category, as in earlier versions.

adjust

character. multiplicity correction method: "none", "bonferroni", "holm" or "BH". With `"none"`, the supplied intervals and E-values are used unchanged. `"holm"` and `"BH"` stop under the default interval rule: margot builds their intervals at coverage 1 - adjusted p, so the intervals exclude the null whatever the adjusted p-value and cannot carry an interval decision. `category_rule = "interval_and_evalue"` still runs them, with a warning, to reproduce earlier output; it carries the same limitation.

alpha

numeric. significance level for corrections

...

other parameters as in original function

options

Plotting options; explicit arguments override corresponding option entries. `colors` may name the levels `"positive"`, `"includes null"` and `"negative"`; a colour named `"not reliable"` is used for `"includes null"` when that level has no colour of its own. `point_shapes` (default up-triangle 24, circle 21 and down-triangle 25 for above, including and below the null) repeats the category in the point shape; `NULL` draws one filled circle for every point, as earlier versions did. `coefficient_colour` (default `"black"`) colours the printed coefficients; `NULL` colours them by category, as earlier versions did. `coefficient_header` (default `"Estimate"`) heads the coefficient column; `NULL` omits it. `text_size` (default 3.5; 2.75 earlier) sets their size. `x_lim_lo` and `x_lim_hi` set the ends of the x range; by default the range is fitted to the null and every estimate and interval limit, with 10% padding (earlier versions fixed the difference-scale range at -0.5 to 0.5). The coefficients form a column inside the panel, drawn from each row's own estimate, so legends, facet strips, faceting, ordering and `coord_flip()` keep them with their outcomes; the "Estimate" header sits at the foot of the column. With the fitted default range the column sits in a band at the left of the panel, and the range is widened to the left when the intervals would run under it. User limits are honoured exactly and the column sits at the left edge of the drawn range; if intervals then run under it, that follows from the chosen range. A supplied `x_offset` places the column there. `x_lim_lo = -0.5`, `x_lim_hi = 0.5` and `x_offset = -0.5` reproduce the earlier difference-scale layout.

label_mapping

Optional mapping from source outcome names to display labels.

save_output

Whether to save the complete reporting list.

use_timestamp

Whether to append a timestamp to saved filenames.

base_filename

Base name for the saved reporting object.

prefix

Optional saved-filename prefix.

save_path

Directory for saved output.

original_df

Legacy unstandardised source data for inferred scale metadata. Explicit saved metadata is preferred.

bold_rows

Whether table row labels whose E-value bound passes the reporting threshold (under `e_val_bound_comparison`) receive Markdown emphasis.

rename_cols

Whether to apply the requested table column-name mapping.

col_renames

Named mapping from new table column names to existing names.

rename_ate

Whether to rename the estimate column, or a supplied replacement name.

rename_evalue

Whether to use display names for E-value columns. The default `"report"` table already uses display names, so this argument affects only `table_columns = "legacy"`.

scale_info

Optional data frame keyed by the original outcome name, with transformation (`identity`, `log`, or `log1p`), saved `center` and positive `scale`, `orientation` (1 or -1), `unit`, and positive `unit_multiplier`. Constants describe the model outcome as orientation * (g(Y) - center) / scale. Explicit metadata overrides inference from `original_df`.

category_rule

How estimates are classified for colour, legend, table and prose. `"interval"` (default) uses the (adjusted) confidence interval alone: above the null, below the null, or including the null. `"interval_and_evalue"` reproduces margot 1.3.2 and earlier, for reproducing earlier results only: an estimate is "positive" or "negative" only when its interval excludes the null and its E-value bound passes the threshold, and is otherwise labelled "not reliable"; the prose then lists only estimates whose bound passes the threshold.

e_val_bound_comparison

Comparison between the E-value bound and `e_val_bound_threshold`: `">"` (default) flags a bound that exceeds the threshold; `">="` reproduces margot 1.3.2 and earlier, which also flagged a bound equal to it. The comparison uses full precision.

e_val_bound_conversion

How the E-value bound is computed from the adjusted interval of a difference-scale estimate when `adjust` is not `"none"`. `"exact"` (default) converts the limit nearest the null directly, RR = exp(0.91 |d_limit|); `"rounded"` reproduces margot 1.3.2 and earlier, for reproducing earlier results only (see [margot_correct_combined_table()]). Not used when `adjust = "none"`.

order_direction

Where the ordering starts. `"top_to_bottom"` (default) draws the first outcome of `order` at the top. `"bottom_to_top"` reproduces margot 1.3.2 and earlier, for reproducing earlier results only: the first outcome was drawn at the bottom, so `"magnitude_desc"` put the largest effect at the bottom. The table and prose follow the plot from top to bottom under either value.

table_columns

Layout of `transformed_table`. `"report"` (default) gives named reporting columns, described under Value. `"legacy"` reproduces the columns of margot 1.3.2 and earlier, for reproducing earlier results only: the effect column, interval columns headed by their quantiles (for example `"0.21 %"`), `confidence_level`, `E_Value`, `E_Val_bound` and the `reported_*` and `reporting_*` columns.

Value

An invisible list with `plot`, `interpretation`, and `transformed_table`.

With the default `table_columns = "report"`, `transformed_table` has one row per outcome, ordered as in the plot from top to bottom. Its row names repeat the `"Outcome"` column (including any emphasis from `bold_rows`), so code that reads `rownames()` keeps working; when printing with `knitr::kable()`, pass `row.names = FALSE` to show the labels once. Numbers keep full precision. Its columns are: `"Outcome"`, the display label (in Markdown bold when `bold_rows = TRUE` and the E-value flag is set); the model-scale estimate (for example `"ATE (standardised)"`); its interval limits (for example `"99.58% CI lower"`, or `"CI lower"` with a `"CI level"` column when coverage varies by outcome); when `scale_info` or `original_df` is supplied, the original-scale estimate and limits, headed by the quantity and unit when every outcome shares them (for example `"Mean difference (scale points)"`, or `"Mean difference (original scale)"` without a unit) and otherwise followed by an `"Original-scale quantity"` column; the decision, headed by the interval and the null (for example `"99.58% CI relative to 0"`, with values `"above 0"`, `"includes 0"` or `"below 0"`; `"Estimate"` under the legacy category rule); `"E-value"`; `"E-value bound"`; and the E-value flag (`"yes"` or `"no"`), headed by the comparison, for example `"E-value bound > 1.1"`. Two columns never share a header: a clash, for example from `rename_ate`, stops with an error.

Details

The statistical decision and the E-value flag are reported separately. By default the decision for each outcome follows its (adjusted) confidence interval alone, and the E-value flag records whether the interval's E-value bound exceeds `e_val_bound_threshold`. The flag sits beside the decision and does not change the plotted colour, legend, table decision or which outcomes the prose lists. The prose lists every outcome whose interval excludes the null, in plot order, with its E-value bound and flag, and names the correction and confidence level. An outcome without both interval limits has no decision: the prose names it, the table reports "not available", and the figure omits it with a message.

To reproduce output from margot 1.3.2 and earlier, set `category_rule = "interval_and_evalue"`, `e_val_bound_comparison = ">="`, `e_val_bound_conversion = "rounded"`, `order_direction = "bottom_to_top"` and `table_columns = "legacy"`. Each argument restores one behaviour and can be set on its own. Together they reproduce the categories, plotted values, table and prose of margot 1.3.2; the figure keeps the current styling (legend centred on the figure, point shapes, black coefficients and sentence-case axis titles), which `options = list(point_shapes = NULL, coefficient_colour = NULL, coefficient_header = NULL, text_size = 2.75)` partly restores. For ratio estimates under `"magnitude_desc"` or `"magnitude_asc"`, the five options do not restore the earlier order, because the orderings now rank by the absolute log ratio; reproducing that order exactly needs `order = "custom"` with the earlier order.
